belief: Our family has always been this way, and it can't change.
origins: Patterns such as anger, addiction, divorce, poverty, silence, or distance can run for generations, and people often say, “That is just how we are.” Hearing it repeated can make change feel disloyal or impossible.
teaches: God told Israel through Ezekiel that the proverb about sins passing to the next generation would no longer be used, and said, “A son will not bear the iniquity of his father.” Paul writes, “If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!” God promises, “I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you.” Patterns do shape us, but they are not destiny. One person who changes can begin a new pattern for those who follow.
self_statements: We have never done it differently.
I will end up like them.
errors: Treating “our family” as a fixed identity.
Believing I must either conform or leave.
Feeling stuck and concluding that I am.
questions: Which patterns in my family do I want to keep, and which do I want to change?
Has anyone in my family broken a pattern, even partly?
What would a first small change look like?
What does it mean to be a new creation?
Who could support me in changing?
What would I want my children or the next generation to say about me?
truth: Family patterns are real, but they are not destiny. In Christ I am a new creation, and God gives me a new heart. I can keep what is good, change what is harmful, and begin a better pattern.
hw_truths: I am a new creation in Christ.
God gives me a new heart.
I can keep the good and change the harmful.
Each person answers for their own choices.
A new pattern can begin with me.
log: Each week, note one thing you did differently from the old pattern.
actions: Write what to keep and what to change.
Tell a pastor or friend what you are trying.
When you slip, apologize and begin again.
prayer: Lord, change begins with You. Give me a new heart, show me what to keep and what to leave, and make me the beginning of something healthier for my family. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I want to keep?
What do I hope for the next generation?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I am a new creation in Christ, not a copy of the past.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Our family has always been this way, and it can't change.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
